confidence.formula: conf = round(S x A x F x G, 2), 0 to 1

S_source_count.note: count of member parts present after tier selection

A_agreement.levels: max(0.3, 1 - min(1, cv / 0.25)); cv = weighted stdev / weighted mean of normalized parts
A_agreement.rates: max(0.3, 1 - min(1, spread_pp / 10)); trend parts with opposite signs cap A at 0.4
A_agreement.forecast: 1.0, times 0.7 when the sign disagrees with value_trend_1y
A_agreement.derived: min of the input metric confidences (S, A, F, G not applied again)

confidence.F_freshness: blend-weighted mean over used parts of 0.5 ** (age_months / half_life_months); age from the source's as_of period end to the run date
confidence.fallback_cap: a value from tier 2 or lower caps conf at 0.45, so it reads low (0.4 for safety on the homicide proxy alone)

blend.weighted_median: weight w_i = base weight x F_i x G_i (x sample factor); weighted median of tier-1 parts
blend.tiered_weighted_median: weighted median of the best non-empty tier; lower tiers never mix with a higher one
blend.first_present: first member by order that has a value; the others set S and A only
blend.percentile_weighted_median: each part becomes a national percentile among ZIPs with a value (pctile_lower inverts), then weighted median; result 0 to 100

normalize.sales_floor_10: weight x 0.4 when the period's homes sold < 10
normalize.roll_forward_value: x fhfa_zip3_index_ratio scaled from the part's period midpoint
normalize.roll_forward_rent: x (1 + rent_trend_1y/100) per year since the ACS midpoint (2022-07)
normalize.roll_forward_income: x (1 + bea_per_capita_income_5y_cagr/100) per year from the ACS midpoint (2022-07) to the middle of the latest year BEA reports (county per-capita income, 5-year annual rate; the state's median rate where the county has none but the state has rates, as in Virginia, Hawaii and Alaska; the national median where the state has none, as in Connecticut and Puerto Rico); never past BEA's own year
normalize.list_to_sale: list_price x sale_to_list / 100, only with active >= 10
normalize.metro_ratio_zori: x median(rent_zori / that field) over the metro's ZIPs with both
normalize.min3_listings: kept with any count; S from the listing count

blend.parts_kept: Each ZIP's shard record keeps m[metric] = {v, c, n, p: [[field, weight, tier], ...]}; member values stay in their own fields, so blended values keep their parts.
blend.area_fallback: Thin ZIPs (Blender.area_fallback, 2026-11-17): a metric with `area_fallback` fills a ZIP it left empty (no source, or nulled by the validity table) from a larger area. First the county value: the listing-weighted median (how weighted_median) or mean (how weighted_mean) over the ZIPs of the ZIP's county that kept their own valid value, weight `weight` (inventory). Else the median of the metro context fields listed in `metro` that the build has (skipped when absent), range-checked. conf = the area value's conf x the geography factor of the area (county 0.6, metro 0.4, G_geography), capped at 0.45 (fallback_cap); a county value's conf is the listing-weighted median of its ZIPs' confs, a metro value's S x F. The shard parts are {v, c, n, p, from: county | metro, area: county FIPS | CBSA}, plus listings for a county value and zip_reason when the ZIP's own value was nulled. A fallback value is shown in the ZIP table but never enters a metro, state or US rollup or a score (h_score and the segment scores read only a ZIP's own values). Counts are never filled from a larger area: inventory stays null.

validity.note: A value outside its allowed range, or without the least evidence it needs, is written null with a short reason, never clamped to a bound. A value computed from a nulled input is null with that input's reason. Checks run in order; the first that fails gives the reason. Keys are metric ids, derived field names (fields.json kind derived) or source fields; a source field is checked before any blend, percentile or derived field reads it. A check's range is min and max, inclusive; min_listings needs the ZIP's inventory (homes for sale) at least that, and an unknown count fails it with reason_unknown when the check sets one (source fields cannot use min_listings: inventory is blended later); if_pop_at_least and if_pop_below limit a check to ZIPs by population (unknown counts as 0); max_ratio_to fails a value more than max_ratio times another field of the ZIP or under 1 / max_ratio of it (no check when that field is missing).
validity.where: The ZIP record's m[name] is {v: null, reason, from} for a nulled metric, source field or derived field (from names the nulled input when inherited); manifest metrics[id] carries limits (these checks) and nulled ({reason: ZIPs}); manifest methods.validity repeats this table with the counts of every nulled name.

follows.note: Legacy fields computed from the same published inputs as a metric (the v1 columns kept in v2 and used as grade factors) are null with that metric's reason where the metric was nulled: 11930's annual rent as share of income read 1,010.1% from the seasonal rent the rent rule rejected.

home_value.why: SeeData D2: 45 ZIPs under $20,000 (62927 at $1) are placeholder or artifact values; gross yield, GRM and affordability follow

typical_rent.why: SeeData D3: the 7 ZORI rents over $20,000 a month are the Hamptons East End (11930 $103,750 to 11954 $27,500, gross yields 12 to 37%), summer rentals read as monthly; the next value is Aspen at $17,626 with a 5.9% yield like its luxury peers, so the cap sits in the gap

gross_yield.why: SeeData D2: yields over 30% under 1,000 people are small-sample noise; over 1,000 people they stay (East St Louis 48%)

days_on_market.why: SeeData D4: 238 ZIPs over a year, up to 9,581 days

price_cuts.why: SeeData D1: 92% of ZIPs with under 5 listings read 0%

income.why: SeeData D10: campus and group-quarters ZIPs (33139 $5,844, 60425 $706); affordability follows
SeeData D10 follow-up: a blended income more than twice or under half the Census survey's median household income (hh_income) is not a reading; the roll-forward fix leaves almost none

lodes_daytime_pop.why: SeeData D12: 327 ZIPs where resident workers exceed residents plus jobs (92092 -565); daytime_pop and lodes_daytime_ratio follow

redfin_cancel_rate.why: SeeData phase 4: Redfin cancellations as a share of pending sales reach 288.7% in 27 ZIPs (more cancellations than pending sales in the window); market heat then ranks without it

metrics.fallback: tier 2 (Realtor median list x sale-to-list, only with 10+ active listings) only when tier 1 is empty
metrics.note: Survey and appraisal levels are rolled forward with fhfa_zip3_index_ratio from their period midpoint.

metrics.label: Home value forecast, 12 months
metrics.note: One source: conf = 0.6 x F x G, times 0.7 when the forecast sign disagrees with value_trend_1y.

metrics.label: Typical rent
metrics.fallback: tier 2 weighted median when ZORI is absent; a tier-2 value caps conf at 0.45
metrics.note: metro_ratio_zori: multiply by the median ZORI / SAFMR ratio of the metro's ZIPs that have both (state ratio outside metros).

metrics.label: Gross rent yield
metrics.formula: typical_rent x 12 / home_value x 100; conf = min(conf of both)

metrics.label: Homes for sale
metrics.note: Definitions differ (active now, end of month, 3-month): headline is the first present; the others only set agreement.

metrics.label: Days to sell
metrics.fallback: Realtor days listed (active listings) only when no sold-home measure exists; a ZIP with no value takes its county's value, else its metro's (area_fallback)

metrics.label: Listings with a price cut
metrics.fallback: a ZIP with no value takes its county's value, else its metro's (area_fallback)

metrics.label: Monthly payment as share of income
metrics.formula: Monthly principal and interest on 80% of home_value (20% down) at mortgage_30y (Freddie Mac 30-year fixed, FRED) over 360 months, plus home_value x property_tax_rate / 1200 when the ZIP's effective property tax rate is known (the parts then list property_tax_rate), divided by monthly household income (income / 12), x 100. r = mortgage_30y / 1200; P&I = 0.8 x home_value x r / (1 - (1 + r) ^ -360). conf = min(conf of home_value, income)

metrics.label: Effective property tax rate
metrics.note: Check only: irs_re_tax_per_itemizer / home_value; a gap over 30% halves A.

metrics.label: People moving in
metrics.note: ZIP-level USPS moves end mid-2023, so they carry the lowest weight and decay by freshness.

metrics.label: Household income
metrics.note: ratio_to_national: scale by the national median of hh_income / that field. roll_forward_income: x (1 + county BEA per-capita income 5-year annual rate / 100) per year from the ACS midpoint (2022-07) to the middle of BEA's latest year.

metrics.label: School test results
metrics.note: State tests differ, so the grade 3 proficiency percentile ranks a ZIP inside its own state and is not comparable across states. Two school years (2020-21 and 2018-19) weigh the same; where they disagree the agreement factor lowers the confidence.

metrics.fallback: With only the county homicide proxy, conf is capped at 0.4.

metrics.fallback: 5-mile ring when the ZIP has under 3 properties (G = 0.8)

metrics.note: Share of a ZIP's CMBS properties on loans 30 days or more late or non-performing at maturity, among properties whose loan reports a payment status. Confidence is multiplied by that reporting share; a ZIP where no loan reports a status has no value.

metrics.note: US-level context for the Commercial page header; not blended or ranked.

retail_score.min_inputs: present weight >= 0.5 and at least 4 inputs

office_score.label: Office property score
office_score.min_inputs: present weight >= 0.5 and at least 4 inputs

industrial_score.label: Industrial property score
industrial_score.min_inputs: present weight >= 0.5 and at least 4 inputs

multifamily_score.universe: ZIPs with population >= 5000 (a real renter base; no merged field counts renter households)
multifamily_score.min_inputs: present weight >= 0.5 and at least 4 inputs

score_rules.percentiles: inputs become percentile ranks (mid-rank ties) within the score's universe; lower-is-better inputs invert; score = weighted mean of present inputs re-weighted over those present
score_rules.missing: a missing input is skipped, never zero; a value a thin ZIP took from its county or metro (area_fallback) counts as missing
score_rules.conf: score conf = present weight share x weighted mean conf of present inputs (metric _conf, or the field's source G x F for raw fields)
score_rules.kept_names: h_score (now v2), c_score (v1 unchanged), area_score/area_grade/area_conf (grade v2), score_parts and grade_parts keep their names; h_score_v1 stays in shards for one release
score_rules.alternates: an input with `or` ranks the first of its fields present at each ZIP (key, then each alternate); the ZIP's score_parts name the field used
score_rules.optional: an input marked optional whose fields this build does not produce at all (a source not landed yet) leaves the score's total weight, so the other inputs re-weight and no ZIP's coverage drops; once any ZIP has it, it counts like every input
score_rules.multifamily_inputs: 2026-11-17: multifamily_score adds renters in buildings of 5+ units (acsmf_renter_5plus_share, ACS 5-year ZCTA, higher), multifamily rent growth (zm_zori_mf_yoy, Zillow ZORI multifamily by metro, higher), metro rental vacancy (hvsm_rental_vacancy, Census HVS, else a1m_rental_vacancy, ACS 1-year metro; lower) and permits for 5+ unit buildings per 1,000 people (mf_permits_5plus_per_1k: county bps_units_5plus_12m, else metro bpm_units_5plus_12m, over the population of the area it was published for; lower). All four are optional with weights 0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 0.05 on top of the base 1.0, re-weighted over the inputs present. fham_upb_maturing_5y (FHA multifamily loan balance maturing in 5 years) is shown in the segment tables, not scored: maturing debt is a refinance signal whose direction for an investor is not settled.

rollup_rules.note: How a ZIP field becomes a metro, state or US value (writer.v2_rollups, 2026-11-17). Every field rolls up by the default for its source level and agg (`default`); a state or metro row's `method` map names only a field rolled up another way (an area field that fell back to its ZIPs, see `fallback`). The v1 fields keep aggregate_method and their v1 entries in `method`.

tract.sum: sum_tracts (when copied or averaged down; apportioned tract counts sum over ZIPs)

default.metric: the metric's `rollup` (sum) when it has one, else pop_weighted_median

rollup_rules.sum_counties: a field its source publishes by county with agg sum: the sum of the published county values, each county once (a county belongs to its FIPS state and to the metro most of its ZIP population lies in). Before, a county value copied to each of its ZIPs was summed over ZIPs (California GDP read $729 trillion).
rollup_rules.sum_tracts: a tract field with agg sum that was copied or averaged down (xwalk assign or mean): the sum of the published tract values, each tract once
rollup_rules.county_pop_weighted_mean: a county field with agg pop_weighted_mean: the mean of the county values weighted by county population (the sum of its ZIPs' ACS population)
rollup_rules.county_pop_weighted_median: the same as a weighted median
rollup_rules.sum: a metric with rollup sum (counts and totals: inventory, population, business_base, jobs, daytime_pop, deposits, building footprint): the sum over the ZIPs with their own value; _n says how many ZIPs entered, so a sum over few ZIPs reads as partial
rollup_rules.pop_weighted_median: every other metric and every score (h_score, retail, office, industrial, multifamily): the population-weighted median over the ZIPs with their own value; <id>_conf is the median ZIP confidence and <id>_n the ZIPs that entered
rollup_rules.fallback: a row no county of which reported (Connecticut's planning regions match no ZIP county) rolls an area field up over ZIPs when that is sound (a weighted mean, or a sum of apportioned shares); a sum of copied county values stays null
rollup_rules.area_fallback: metric values a thin ZIP took from its county or metro (blend.area_fallback) never enter a rollup

rental_grade.label: Rental area grade v2 (fields area_score, area_grade, area_conf, grade_parts, grade_flags keep their names)
rental_grade.conf: area_conf = present weight share x weighted mean conf of the factors present (v1 used present weight only)
